instantiation.worst_case: Every `hello.v1.HelloService/Hello` call whose `name` is empty or whitespace, which previously succeeded with `"hello "`, now fails with gRPC `InvalidArgument` (code 3). Blast radius as measured: one cluster, `e1-dev`, one ready pod (instances query: {cluster=e1-dev} 1), service type ClusterIP only (exposure query: hello, hello-canary both ClusterIP — nothing reachable from outside the cluster), and exactly one caller, workload `traffic` in namespace `frontend` under principal spiffe://cluster.local/ns/frontend/sa/frontend at ~1.5 rps (callers query). No prod or staging instance appears in any measured series, and discover.yaml answers record staging_exists=no. So the realistic worst case is: the single internal traffic generator (and, later, the real `frontend` service listed in service.yaml authorizedCallers) starts receiving code 3 on blank-name requests; because the canary AnalysisTemplate `server-errors` (deploy/base/rollout.yaml) counts only code=~"Unknown|Internal|DataLoss|DeadlineExceeded", a 100%-InvalidArgument regression would not fail the canary gate and, with no alerting rules in the metrics stack (discover.yaml stack.metrics), nothing would page. Secondary worst case: if CI's e2e probe or the toxic-client conformance suite asserts the old empty-name response, the change never ships (red CI) rather than breaking production.

Also confirm the author's description matches the diff (it does claim trim + InvalidArgument) and that `google.golang.org/grpc/status` and `codes` are already available at the module version in go.mod (no go.mod/go.sum edit is in this PR — if the imports are not already satisfied, the build fails).
